input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The doors are supposed to open at nine, and the tables will be ready by 8:15. The hall manager said the side entrance can be unlocked at eight if someone from our group is there to meet him; otherwise, everybody has to use the front steps. The ramp is on the north side, and we should leave that route clear because two regular visitors use walkers. The exchange is free, and people can bring saved seeds or take packets without bringing anything. The idea is to make it friendly for first-time gardeners as well as people who have been growing here for years.

The room has twelve folding tables, and we have permission to use ten of them. The other two need to stay against the west wall for the quilting group that meets in the afternoon. Please put the vegetable packets near the windows because the light is good there, but keep them out of direct sun if the curtains are open. The herb table will be beside the water fountain, and flowers will go across from the entrance. We need a clear aisle from the door to the back of the room and a smaller gap between each table so people can move without brushing the displays. The hall has three extension cords, but we should only use one for the label printer and tape it along the wall, not across a walking route.

The exchange team has four main jobs, and I want to say them slowly: first, receiving and checking packets; second, setting up the tables; third, greeting people and keeping track of shared supplies; and fourth, closing the room and returning the key. Priya is the packet lead, and Noah is checking the sign-in sheets. Priya will bring the blank labels and the small scale, and she will sort anything with no crop name into a question box rather than guessing what it is. Sam is handling the table plan and has a printed map in the green folder. Jo is greeting people at the front table, and I will keep the supply list and be available if a volunteer needs a break.

Packets should be dry and sealed and should have enough seeds for at least five small gardens. If someone brings a large envelope, Priya can divide it after asking them first. We are not refusing packets just because the handwriting is hard to read. She can ask the donor or write a question mark on the label if nobody knows the variety. Please do not describe a seed as organic unless the person who saved it says that is accurate, and do not promise that a packet will grow in every yard. We can offer general information, but the weather and soil make a difference.

The three supplies we still need to borrow are a folding hand truck, two extra marker pens, and a small tablecloth for the welcome desk. We have enough paper bags but only about forty blank labels, so Priya will print another sheet on Thursday evening. Sam has offered to bring masking tape and scissors, and the library is lending us two clipboards. The packet count from the storage cabinet is 1,138, but some of those packets are herbs that need a closer check. The printed inventory says 963 vegetable packets, and the handwritten notebook lists 175 flowers and herbs. Those totals match for now, but we should count the question box separately and not include it in the public totals.

When people arrive, Jo can say, “Take what you will use and leave some for the next person.” We are not asking visitors to fill out a form, and there is no limit per person at the moment. If the room gets crowded, she can ask people to step aside while another visitor reaches the table, but we should not start enforcing a packet limit unless the organizers talk it through together. The neighborhood garden club may bring six children around 10:30, and their teacher has asked whether they can sit at one end of the flower table while they sort their packets. We can make room for them if the aisle stays open and an adult remains with the group.

First, for the morning setup, lay down the table map and check the aisle. Second, put the signs on the right tables and place the question box beside Priya. Third, set out packets with the labels facing up and leave the handwritten inventory in the green folder. Fourth, keep the welcome desk clear except for the clipboards and a cup for spare pencils. At 11:30, someone should check whether the water jug needs filling, and after lunch we should gather loose labels and return markers to the supply box. Those are reminders rather than extra jobs, and nobody needs to leave their station unattended to do them.

One condition that matters is the forecast. If there is heavy rain before 8:30, we will not put the two outdoor display boards on the pavement, even if the sky clears later, because the boards can become slippery and the hall manager asked us to protect the floor. In that case, we can put the garden club poster inside by the noticeboard. If there is only light rain, the boards may go under the covered porch as long as the front entrance remains unobstructed. Sam is checking the forecast Friday evening and will text the team, but that message is only about the boards, not a change to the opening time.

At closing, we need to leave the ten tables folded only after the packets and supplies are collected, and the west wall must remain clear for the quilting group. We should return the key to the lockbox by 4:15 and send the manager a message once the door is locked. Any seeds that remain can go back into the labeled storage tubs on the top shelf, except the question box, which stays separate until Priya has checked with the donors. If someone leaves a phone number with a packet question, Jo can put that note in the green folder, and we can follow up after the exchange. The final count and a note about any missing supplies belong in the notebook before we leave."}]
